title: Nine Votes
subtitle: A council seat decided by nine votes, and two camps at the counting hall
coldOpen: 02:10. The ward count ends: a nine-vote margin.
06:00. The losing side demands a full recount.
Both sides are gathering at the counting hall.

briefing.grievance: The trailing candidate’s agents say two bundles were counted twice. The leading side says the count is final and any delay is theft. The hall is between them.
knownFacts: The declared margin is nine votes out of 11,400.
Both candidates’ agents signed the station-level sheets last night.
The rules allow a recount application within 24 hours of the declaration.
unverifiedClaims: A message says ballot bundles were moved after the agents left.
A post says the returning officer has already destroyed the rejected ballots.
briefing.responsibility: You are the returning officer with police support. The count must be right, and both sides must be able to see that it is.
briefing.objective: Decide on the recount by the rules, in the open, and keep two crowds apart.

decisions.title: Two camps, one hall
decisions.situation: Supporters of both candidates are arriving at the counting hall. Agents from both sides are inside asking what happens next.

options.title: Read the rules and the timeline to both camps
options.preview: The recount window, the seal status and today’s steps, announced at the gate.
options.authority: Duty of candour: say what is known and what is not
options.consequence: Both camps hear the same timeline. The shouting drops to questions.

options.title: Bring both agents to the table
options.preview: The agents sit with you and the seal log; nothing happens without both present.
options.authority: Duty to hear grievances; Article 19(1)(a) free expression
options.consequence: Both agents are at the table. Their supporters watch them, not each other.

options.title: Declare the result final and clear the gate
options.preview: No recount; police move both camps away from the hall.
options.authority: Article 19(2)–(3): restrictions must be reasonable and specific
options.consequence: The losing side is cleared before its application is read. The hall looks like it has something to hide.

delayed.message: The crackdown hardens people who had stayed out of it. More arrive, angrier.

options.title: Keep the hall shut and silent
options.preview: Nobody explains anything; both camps grow.
options.consequence: The hall looks shut, not sealed.

simple.title: Two sides, one hall
simple.situation: Supporters of both candidates are arriving. The agents inside want to know what happens next.

o-d004-1-rules.title: Read the rules to both sides
o-d004-1-rules.preview: The recount rule, the seal and today’s steps, said at the gate.
o-d004-1-rules.consequence: Both sides hear the same plan. Shouting turns into questions.

o-d004-1-agents.title: Sit both agents at the table
o-d004-1-agents.preview: Both agents sit with you and the seal log.
o-d004-1-agents.consequence: Supporters watch their agents, not each other.

o-d004-1-declare.title: Declare it final, clear the gate

o-d004-1-declare.consequence: The losing side is cleared before being heard.

o-d004-1-wait.title: Keep the hall shut and silent
o-d004-1-wait.preview: Nobody explains anything. Both crowds grow.
o-d004-1-wait.consequence: The hall looks shut, not safe.

decisions.title: Stations 7 and 12
decisions.situation: The application is specific. Table 7’s camera shows bundles restacked with agents present. The footage expires in two days.

options.title: Order a recount of stations 7 and 12 in the open
options.preview: Both agents, two observers and a camera at the table this afternoon.
options.authority: Due process: establish the facts before acting on them
options.consequence: Two stations are recounted under everyone’s eyes.

options.title: Preserve the footage; reseal every bundle
options.preview: Camera files copied; every bundle resealed with both agents initialling.
options.authority: Duty to keep essential services running
options.consequence: Nothing can be moved or lost now. The record is safe.

options.title: Call the double-count claim an invention
options.preview: A statement calls the application a fabrication.
options.authority: Due process: a public charge needs verified evidence
options.consequence: The statement goes out before anyone has looked at table 7.

options.title: Decide on the recount tomorrow
options.preview: The window narrows; the camera footage keeps aging.

simple.title: Stations 7 and 12
simple.situation: The request names two tables. The camera shows restacking with both sides there. The clip expires soon.

o-d004-2-recount.title: Recount stations 7 and 12 openly
o-d004-2-recount.preview: Both agents, two watchers and a camera at the table today.
o-d004-2-recount.consequence: Two stations are recounted with everyone watching.

o-d004-2-preserve.title: Save the footage, reseal bundles
o-d004-2-preserve.preview: Copy the camera files. Reseal every bundle with both sides.
o-d004-2-preserve.consequence: Nothing can be moved or lost now.

o-d004-2-accuse.title: Say the losing side made it up
o-d004-2-accuse.preview: A statement calls the request a lie.
o-d004-2-accuse.consequence: It goes out before anyone checks table 7.

o-d004-2-wait.title: Decide tomorrow
o-d004-2-wait.preview: Time runs out. The footage gets older.
o-d004-2-wait.consequence: Both sides camp outside all night.

decisions.title: Supporters face each other
decisions.situation: The two camps are now a street apart, chanting. The seal log is clean. A line of officers stands between them.

options.title: Same written terms for both camps
options.preview: Equal hours, marshals and distances for both sides, announced together.
options.authority: Article 19(1)(b): peaceful assembly, policed in proportion
options.consequence: Both camps get identical rules. Neither can claim favour.

options.title: Separate the few throwing stones
options.preview: Officers pull out the stone-throwers only; both camps stay.
options.authority: Proportionality: act against the few causing harm, not the many
options.consequence: The stone-throwers are gone. The crowds stay where they are.

options.title: Ban all gatherings near the hall
options.preview: Both camps are cleared and a 500-metre no-gathering zone is declared.
options.authority: Article 19(2)–(3): restrictions must be reasonable and specific
options.consequence: Two lawful gatherings are gone. Both sides say the count is being hidden.

delayed.message: The crackdown hardens people who had stayed out of it. More arrive, angrier.

options.title: Hold the line and hope
options.preview: The officers stand; the chanting continues all afternoon.

simple.title: The two sides face off
simple.situation: The camps are a street apart, chanting. Police stand between them.

o-d004-3-terms.title: Same rules for both sides
o-d004-3-terms.preview: Equal hours, marshals and distances, said to both at once.
o-d004-3-terms.consequence: Both sides get the same rules.

o-d004-3-targeted.title: Remove only the stone-throwers
o-d004-3-targeted.preview: Officers take out the few throwing stones.
o-d004-3-targeted.consequence: They are gone. The crowds stay.

o-d004-3-ban.title: Ban all gatherings near the hall
o-d004-3-ban.preview: Both sides are cleared from 500 metres around.
o-d004-3-ban.consequence: Two lawful crowds are gone. Both say the count is hidden.

o-d004-3-wait.title: Hold the line and hope
o-d004-3-wait.preview: Officers stand there. Chanting goes on all afternoon.

decisions.title: Declaring the result

options.title: Declare with the full reconciliation attached
options.preview: Station totals, the recount outcome and the seal log, published together.
options.authority: Duty of candour: say what is known and what is not

options.title: Brief both candidates privately first
options.preview: Each candidate hears the outcome before the public does.
options.authority: Duty to hear grievances; Article 19(1)(a) free expression
options.consequence: The candidates tell their own supporters. The street hears it from them.

options.title: Blame the trailing side for the day’s disorder
options.preview: The declaration adds a paragraph calling the recount demand a stunt.
options.authority: Due process: a public charge needs verified evidence
options.consequence: A lawful application is called a stunt in an official document.

options.title: Delay the declaration overnight
options.preview: No numbers; both camps stay another night.

simple.title: Declaring the result
simple.situation: The recount is done or not. The seal is intact. Both sides wait.

o-d004-4-declare.title: Declare with all the numbers
o-d004-4-declare.preview: Every station total, the recount result and the seal log, together.
o-d004-4-declare.consequence: Both sides can check every number.

o-d004-4-brief.title: Tell both candidates first
o-d004-4-brief.preview: Each candidate hears the result before the public.
o-d004-4-brief.consequence: The candidates tell their own people.

o-d004-4-accuse.title: Blame the losing side for the trouble
o-d004-4-accuse.preview: The result adds a line calling the recount request a stunt.
o-d004-4-accuse.consequence: A lawful request is called a stunt.

o-d004-4-wait.title: Delay until tomorrow
o-d004-4-wait.preview: No numbers. Both sides stay another night.

decisions.title: “Announce the winner now and end this”
decisions.situation: The leading camp, and your phone, want the result declared this minute to “stop the chaos”.

options.title: Declare now, recount refused
options.preview: The winner is announced; the application is dismissed unread.
options.authority: Article 19(2)–(3): restrictions must be reasonable and specific
options.consequence: The street believes the count was never checked.

delayed.message: The losing camp calls the declaration a cover-up and marches on the hall.

options.title: Announce the recount time instead
options.preview: A notice: “Recount of two stations at 3 pm, both agents present.”
options.authority: Duty of candour: say what is known and what is not
options.consequence: The timetable is the announcement. Both camps have something to wait for.

options.title: Let the pressure build
options.consequence: The leading camp calls the delay theft.

simple.title: “Announce the winner now”
simple.situation: The winning side wants the result declared this minute.

o-d004-bait-declare.title: Announce the winner now
o-d004-bait-declare.preview: The winner is declared. The request is thrown out unread.
o-d004-bait-declare.consequence: The street believes the count was never checked.

o-d004-bait-time.title: Announce the recount time
o-d004-bait-time.preview: A notice says: recount at 3 pm, both sides present.

o-d004-bait-wait.title: Say nothing
o-d004-bait-wait.consequence: The winning side calls it theft.

rightsMoments.question: Two rival groups want to gather near the counting hall. What rules may you set?

options.text: The same reasonable conditions for both: times, distances, marshals.
options.feedback: Correct. Equal treatment means equal rules, not equal outcomes.

options.text: Allow only the leading side, because its claim is now official.
options.feedback: An official result does not remove the other side’s right to assemble peacefully.

options.text: Ban both, since any gathering near a count is a risk.
options.feedback: A blanket ban is not a reasonable restriction when conditions can manage the risk.

rightsMoments.principle: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law. Article 19(1)(b) protects peaceful assembly, subject only to reasonable, even-handed restrictions.
rightsMoments.why: In a disputed count, treating the camps differently would have been read as the count itself being rigged.

simple.question: Two rival groups want to gather near the hall. What rules can you make?

options.a: The same fair rules for both: times, distances, marshals.
options.b: Let only the winning side gather.

feedback.a: Yes! Equal rules for both sides.
feedback.b: No. Winning does not take away the other side’s right.
feedback.c: A total ban is too much when rules can keep it safe.

simple.principle: The law treats everyone the same. Both sides may gather peacefully under the same rules.
simple.why: If one side got better treatment, people would believe the count was rigged too.

events.message: The hall’s power is cut from the street box. The seal room alarm goes dark.
events.simple: Someone cuts the hall’s power. The alarm goes dark.

events.message: Stones cross the street between the camps. An officer is hit.
events.simple: Stones fly between the two sides.

resolved.text: Two stations were recounted in front of both agents and a camera.
resolved.simple: Two stations were recounted with both sides watching.

resolved.text: Footage and bundles were preserved before anything could go missing.
resolved.simple: Footage and bundles were kept safe.

resolved.text: The result was declared with every number attached.
resolved.simple: The result came with every number attached.

unresolved.text: The result was declared before the application was examined.
unresolved.simple: The result was declared before the request was checked.

unresolved.text: The table-7 footage was never secured.
unresolved.simple: The camera clip was never saved.

unresolved.text: No reconciliation was published; both sides still argue about the numbers.
unresolved.simple: No numbers were published. Both sides still argue.

rightsProtected.text: Both camps assembled under identical, published terms.
rightsProtected.simple: Both sides gathered under the same rules.

rightsProtected.text: The losing side’s application was read, not dismissed.
rightsProtected.simple: The losing side was heard, not ignored.

rightsHarmed.text: Lawful gatherings were cleared or banned around the count.
rightsHarmed.simple: Lawful crowds were cleared or banned.

rightsHarmed.text: A timely recount application was refused unread.
rightsHarmed.simple: A proper recount request was thrown out unread.

improvements.text: A specific, timely recount request is a chance to prove the count, not a threat to it.
improvements.simple: A specific recount request is a chance to prove the count.

improvements.text: Secure footage and reseal bundles the moment a count is disputed.
improvements.simple: Save the camera and reseal the bundles right away.

improvements.text: Give both camps the same written rules before either feels favoured.
improvements.simple: Give both sides the same written rules early.

closing.good: The nine votes held, and both sides watched them being counted. The hall was never shut, only sealed.
closing.mixed: The result stands, but one camp still thinks the hall hid something, and the street remembers the stones.
closing.poor: The count was declared before it was checked, and the losing side has every reason to keep asking.
